release.note: Initial content review, source verification (Riis, the 1900 census transcription, the Levine family-story PDF, the NYC LGBT Historic Sites page, the 1903 Tenement House Problem volume and the 97 Orchard National Register form read; three Tenement Museum web pages refused automated access and are no longer relied on), two package review passes and the slate content check complete. known_research_boundaries: A fictional single adult's first-night search in 1900 contrasts nightly lodging, boarding and monthly family housing. Mills House No.1 was operating, and Riis's1900 edition—not only his 1902 rewrite—confirms20c lodging, 15c dinner and shared amenities. The9am–5pm room closure occurs in the 1902 book but was not located in the 1900 passage, so omit it. The 1900 census supplies actual male and female boarders at 97 Orchard, avoiding reliance on a 1908 citywide percentage. Veiller rent ranges belong to a different surveyed block; caption and speech say so.97 Orchard's apartments are small three-room homes, not three-bedroom homes. The Levines have three children in 1900, not the eventual five; workplace staff are not counted as residents. Do not use the Ellis Island main hall without choosing a date after itsDecember 1900 opening, or assume all arrivals passed through it. Avoid 1901 tenement reforms, 1903 women'shotel, 1904 subway, 1909 Mills/bridge imagery. Riis is a reform advocate with stigmatizing prejudices; factual observations can be used without adopting his moral explanations of poverty. No authenticity claim for fictional Visitor's bed or particular family's private agreement. Re-check 2026-10-10: the rent chapter speaks the 1900 Commission's block counts and one witness's rents (SRC08) instead of the museum article's floor ranges, which could not be re-read; the apartment figures follow the National Register form (SRC09) and no whole-building count is spoken because readable sources disagree (20 or 22).
